newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-FOURTEEN TO RUN IN EPSOM DERBY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-FOURTEEN TO RUN IN EPSOM DERBY.

text.p: Fourteen runners were declared on Thursday for Saturday's Epsom Derby, worth over one million pounds for the first time in a history dating back to 1780.
Two horses were withdrawn at the final sstage, leaving hot favourite Entrepreneur, the mount of Michael Kinane, with 13 opponents between him and a place in the record books.

As expected, Grapeshot, who had been quoted at 20-1, was pulled out by trainer Luca Cumani after suffering a slight injury in training. Stowaway, 66-1 outsider, was also withdrawn, leaving the Godolphin operation with only one runner, the 20-1 chance Bold Demand to be ridden by Frankie Dettori.
The Godolphin team, the brainchild of Sheikh Mohammed, has had a brilliant run in the last couple of years winning many major races and classics.
But they suffered a wretched spell in May and at one time there was talk of Saeed Bin Suroor closing down operations for a while to try to sort out whatever problem was ailing their horses.
Butr Bold Demand ended the drought with a success at Sandown last week, a victory impressive enough to earn his place in Saturday's Derby.
Entrepreneur, trained by Michael Stoute, remains the firm favourite on the strength of his 2,000 Guineas win at Newmarket and is clearly the one they all have to beat.

Silver Patriach at 11-2, is the solid second favourite and has behind him the highly experienced team of trainer John Dunlop, seeking his third Derby success, and jockey Pat Eddery, chasing his fourth.
The gamble of the race has been the French raider Cloudings, the mount of Olivier Peslier, who deserted the well-fancied Benny The Dip to take the ride on Andre Fabre's runner.
Cloudings was a 33-1 chance a week ago but is now down to 8-1 joint third-favourite. If Entrepreneur a flaw, the improving Cloudings may be the one to find him out.
A classic two days of action start on Friday with the Epsom Oaks where trainer Henry Cecil has the top two in the betting - Reams of Verse (4-6) and Yashmak (6-1). Twelve fillies go to post.
